releases.body:
# Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6

What's new since 1.9.8.4.

## Picture fixes
- **Smeared picture fixed (two causes):**
  - After a load, the game sometimes rewrote a command buffer it had already handed to the GPU. The picture then stayed broken or smeared until the game was restarted. Every submitted command buffer is now copied first (`BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS=0` turns this off). The same cause was behind "Unimplemented PM4 type 0" and "PM4 header ... rest of the buffer dropped" in logs.
  - After a start with an empty shader cache, one saved pipeline could be lost for the whole next session. The game's motion blur then kept blurring the last frame, so the picture looked smeared and frozen from the first camera turn on.
- Rainbow tiles on hit enemies and a light line along the top in cutscenes are fixed.
- **NaN and infinity:** shaders follow the PS4 GPU's rules where Vulkan leaves NaN and infinity open (min/max, clamping, legacy multiplies, compares). A NaN or infinity written to a float render target becomes 0 or its largest value. releases.name: ARMSX3 for iOS 0.0.2 beta
releases.body:
Changes since 0.0.1. Thanks to everyone who sent problem reports, since most of these fixes came from them. This is a beta: the JIT changes ran on an iPhone, and everything else was tested on a Mac. Please send a report if something works worse than in 0.0.1.

## Requirements and install

ARMSX3 for iOS needs an iPhone or iPad with an A14 chip or newer, on iOS 17.4 or later. It isn't on the App Store, so install the IPA with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. JIT needs a pairing file for your device (see Pairing files below).

## Update LiveContainer first

If you run ARMSX3 inside LiveContainer, update LiveContainer to 3.8.13 or later before you install this build. That is the nightly build at the moment: https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/nightly Older versions can't load the JIT helper, and ARMSX3 will fall back to StikDebug.

In LiveContainer, turn on Helper Process Support for ARMSX3, and open ARMSX3 full screen, not in a window.

## Built-in JIT inside LiveContainer

ARMSX3 can now turn on JIT by itself inside LiveContainer, the same way it already did when installed on its own. You no longer need StikDebug for this. We tested it inside LiveContain

ARMSX3 for iOS is a PlayStation 3 emulator for iPhone and iPad. It runs the same RPCS3-based core as the ARMSX3 Android app, with an app built for iOS around it, and draws through Vulkan on MoltenVK. This is the first build I'm sharing with everyone. Treat it as a beta: some games already play well, many don't yet, and you will run into crashes I haven't seen. When you do, a report helps a lot, and the end of this post explains how to send one.

releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.6.7 Most of this release is @J1coding's work: fixes he found while bringing ARMSX3 to iOS, now on Android too. ## New - **Faster boots**: ARMSX3 now keeps a game's compiled SPU code between boots. The first boot after an update builds it once, and every boot after that loads it. On an Odin 3, Spider-Man: Web of Shadows' SPU step takes 2.5 s instead of 16 s. It lives in ARMSX3's own cache folder on the phone, which Android can clear like any app cache, and it switches itself off when the phone has less than 1 GB free. Done by @J1coding. ## Rare-case fixes - **Leaving a game no longer gets stuck** on memory the graphics side had locked. Picture size, eye spacing and height are adjustable live and per game, from the in-game menu too. Games with stereo 3D give each eye its own view (turn on 3D Display Enabled in All Core Settings, with the PS3 resolution at 1280x720). Done by @k1r4ct. On 8 Elite: - **Sonic the Hedgehog (2006) runs at a locked 60:** a signal the game sends an SPU waits only when the SPU hasn’t read the previous one yet, instead of after every signal. ## Performance and display - **SPU threads with nothing to do stop burning CPU.** Web of Shadows CPU usage went from 70-80 on an 8 Elite

releases.name: melonDualDS 0.7.0 RC5: RetroAchievements Stability Update!
releases.body: # Next release will be WatermelonDS! This release is focused on RetroAchievements stability, Hardcore achievement reliability, leaderboards, and new offline achievement provider options. This will also be the last release using the current **melonDualDS** name. The next release will introduce a new interface, a new icon, and a new experimental Vulkan feature called **FastPath**. FastPath is designed to significantly improve performance at high internal resolutions, even up to 8x in some cases. However, FastPath will be experimental. If you want the most stable and accurate experience, closer to real Nintendo DS behavior, it is recommended to keep FastPath disabled when it becomes available. It will be especially useful for devices with slightly weaker chipsets, or for users who want to get the most performance and battery efficiency possible. This release candidate completes support for the cheat instructions implemented by Eden's DMNT engine and improves cheat-file parsing and process targeting.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc7.

### What's new since rc7

- **Extended cheat instructions:** implemented register comparisons, register save/restore operations and masks, persistent static registers, process pause/resume, and debug logging, with all operand and addressing forms supported by Eden.
- **Cheat execution:** corrected nested if/else handling, loop decoding, arithmetic behavior, and handling of truncated or unknown instructions. Controller input is sampled once per execution so multiple button conditions see the same input state.
- **Cheat files and process targeting:** fixed parsing of names containing Unicode symbols or accents. Memory operations and pause/resume now target the process identified by the cheat metadata, with a cached non-owning process reference.
- **Regression coverage:** 24 cheat-engine tests pass, covering instruction execution, memory widths, pointer chains, branches, loops

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc6
releases.body:
This release candidate fixes an audio-update parsing error that could cause invalid mixer data and audio glitches.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc5.

### What’s new since rc5

- **Audio update parsing:** the audio renderer now respects the splitter block size declared in the update header. Previously, it could read the following mixer block at the wrong offset, resulting in invalid mix counts or rejected audio updates.
- **Input validation:** added bounds checks for declared splitter blocks.
- **Regression coverage:** added synthetic tests covering splitter block boundaries, subsequent mixer updates, and header layout.

This correction addresses a likely cause of the audio errors reported in [issue #21](https://github.com/vricosti/ruzu-emu/issues/21). Confirmation through extended gameplay is still needed.

### Known limitations

Unsupported shader instructions may still cause missing graphics or prevent a scene from rendering. This release does not resolve every freeze, black-screen issue, or audio glitch.

Multi-program game compatibility remains experimental.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes the improvements from rc1, rc2 and rc3.

### What’s new since rc3

- **Game collections:** titles that chain into a sub-program (`ExecuteProgram`) now work. Previously, picking a game from a collection’s menu left the screen frozen at 0 FPS. Ruzu now shuts the running program down and boots the requested program of the same file. 
- **Kernel:** thread termination now signals completion and notifies waiting threads under the scheduler lock, after the terminating thread has left its core. This closes an ordering window between the two notifications.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. ## Android

- **Leaving the game and coming back no longer crashes it.** Home, switching to another app or the screen turning off, then coming back: up to 0.3.18 the return crashed (in `vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR`, with a window Android had already freed). Now the game lets go of the old window when it leaves the screen and connects to the new one when it comes back (SDK patch 0085). Co-op friendly fire, a way out for stuck guests, more settings that apply at once, and Linux fixes. Everything from [0.4.1](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.1) is included.

## New

- **Friendly fire in campaign co-op.** PC Options > Multiplayer > **Friendly fire (co-op)**. It turns on only while **every** player in the session has it on; if one player turns it off, nobody can hurt anybody again. Only human players can hurt each other: AI squadmates never take or deal friendly damage. The host log says `COOPFF active (2/2 opted in)` or `COOPFF inactive (1/2 opted in)`. Split-screen players on one PC share one setting.

releases.body:
A small fix release on top of [0.4.0](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.0): everything from 0.4.0 is included.

## Fixes

- **Blue or white weapons and heads on NVIDIA (#44).** With **Graphics > Renderer > Automatic** (emulated on PC), NVIDIA cards went through the ROV render target path, which drew some held weapons and character heads blue, red or white (seen on an RTX 3070 Ti and an RTX 4070 Ti). At 16:9, Automatic on NVIDIA now uses host render targets, like AMD. Ultrawide and 16:10 keep ROV, because only that path has room for the wider picture. The log says `RTPATH ... render target path set to 'rtv'`. To pick the path yourself, set `render_target_path_d3d12 = "rov"` or `"rtv"` in `gow2.toml`. The first start after updating compiles shaders again, so expect a few short hitches.

Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. **Fixed**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.4

Fourth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. More than 100 games now run correctly according to testers' reports, and this release adds CapyPS5 Framegen. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **CapyPS5 Framegen:** optional frame generation. It draws in-between frames from the motion between two game frames, so a game at 30 FPS is shown at 60. Off by default; turn it on in *Settings → Performance* (1 per frame, or up to 3). Adds one frame of latency and some GPU load; works best from 25 FPS up.
- New performance options in *Settings → Performance*: shadow resolution, early depth testing and a frame rate limit (30 or 20 FPS).
- Physical keyboard input and an on-screen keyboard toggle for text fields, and system dialogs that can now be answered.
- Android 16 and devices with 16 KB memory pages are supported.

**Fixed**
- Unreal Engine 5 games: graphics and async compute hand work back and forth several times per frame, and each hand-off waited up to 100 ms. Menus that ran at 0–2 FPS now move.
- Games whose shadows use depth-compare texture gathers (Castlevania: Belmont's Curse) closed after the menu.
- Games built with MONITORX/MWAITX instru

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.3
releases.body:
Third alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Fixes for the logs testers sent on v0.0.2, CPU work for Unreal Engine games, and more from KytyPS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Fixed**
- Games that use fibers (sceFiber) closed the emulator at start on ARM ("Fiber context switching is only implemented on x86_64", Toy Story Retro Roundup). Fibers now switch the game's own registers. First support: please report how fiber games behave.
- Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: sceKernelFtruncate, which it calls when saving, is now available.
- Mewgenics: pthread_setcanceltype is now available.
- The game clock (RDTSC) ran about 23 % faster than the frequency games are told; they now match.
- Very large GPU compute dispatches (over 65535 groups, as in Astro Bot) are split to fit Adreno limits.
- Unity backtraces no longer follow a bogus frame at the start of each guest thread.

**New**
- Unreal Engine games: the TLS and process clock reads they make millions of times a second run inside the game code instead of calling into the emulator.
- Shaders can read the real GPU clock (S_MEMREALTIME) on drivers that offer it.
- JpegDec and JpegEnc libraries, and more

What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices

  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.
- Network play is not compatible anymore with PC Mod
